Finding: Taxonomic, functional and structural evidence was successfully integrated on the common 90-plot sampling backbone.
Validated structural evidence represents 89.37% of plot-level abundance overall, with explicit structural analysis tiers.
The ecological system is multidimensional: four PCA axes are required to exceed 70% cumulative variance.
Habitat and Management Zone jointly structure taxonomic diversity, functional traits and forest structure, with several responses dominated by interaction effects.
Several ecological domains remain significantly coupled after Habitat/Zone adjustment, especially taxonomic diversity with functional diversity and forest structure.
Taxonomic diversity–functional composition coupling is largely explained by Habitat and Management Zone structure.
Four recurrent integrated ecological states were validated from the 10-metric ecological core.
Core plots are dominated by the Dense-Wood Conservative state and exhibit high wood density with generally low SLA.
Buffer plots are dominated by the Structurally Developed Diverse state and are comparatively intermediate across the ecological indicator space.
Transition plots are dominated by T3/T4 trait syndromes and are characterized overall by lower wood density, higher SLA and lower richness.
Transition Major River exhibits the greatest typology heterogeneity, containing all four validated ecological states.
The final indicator framework supports multidimensional repeat monitoring without requiring a synthetic ecological-condition score.
